deities: Lord Hanuman as Sankat Mochan (remover of troubles)
festivals: Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh (annual 5-day classical music and dance festival)

history.dynasty: 16th-century foundation by Goswami Tulsidas; present structure early 1900s by Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya
history.period: Early 16th century (foundation); present structure early 20th century
history.summary: Founded by the poet-saint Goswami Tulsidas (author of the Ramcharitmanas) at the spot where he is said to have had a divine vision of Lord Hanuman beneath a sacred fig tree near the Assi stream. 'Sankat Mochan' means 'reliever of troubles', and devotees believe prayers here mitigate afflictions, including adverse planetary influences of Shani and Mangal. The present-day structure was built in the early 1900s by freedom fighter and BHU founder Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya; the Sankat Mochan Foundation was started in 1982 by the temple's high priest Veer Bhadra Mishra. On 7 March 2006 a bomb blast struck the temple during aarti, after which a permanent police post was set up. Known for its forest-hermitage atmosphere, resident monkey population, continuous Hanuman Chalisa chanting, and besan-laddoo prasad. Mobile phones and cameras are strictly prohibited.

name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
town_description: Varanasi (Banaras/Kashi) is one of the world's oldest living cities, on the banks of the Ganga in eastern Uttar Pradesh. The temple sits in the southern part of the city near Assi Ghat and Banaras Hindu University, in the Durgakund temple cluster with the Durga and Tulsi Manas temples.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (approx. 25 km; taxis and app cabs).
travel.railway: Varanasi Junction (approx. 8 km); also reachable from Assi Ghat (approx. 2 km).
travel.road: On Assi Ghat Road near BHU; easily reached by auto-rickshaw, taxi and e-rickshaw. Part of the Varanasi southern cluster (Assi Ghat - Sankat Mochan - Tulsi Manas) circuit.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Tuesdays and Saturdays are the most auspicious and most crowded days; the Sankat Mochan Sangeet Samaroh draws renowned classical artists.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open daily 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM; sources conflict on aarti times (morning aarti reported 4:00/4:30/5:00/5:30 AM; evening aarti 7:30/8:00/9:00 PM) — verify. Entry free; mobiles and cameras strictly prohibited (submit outside). Busiest on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
